### Server uptime

**`serverStatus.uptime`** — seconds the current **mongod** process has been running.

**Unit:** seconds (displayed as duration)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.uptime`

---

### How to read

- Monotonic increase while the process is up
- **Drop** or reset → **restart** (mark the timestamp)
- May not start at zero if the dashboard time range begins mid-run

---

### Troubleshooting

- Restart + memory drop → OOM · **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)**, **Swap Memory**
- Restart + assert spike → crash · **Asserts**
- Planned maintenance → correlate with deploy window
- After restart, counters reset · **Operations**, **Page Faults** rates may look odd briefly

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)

### WiredTiger ticket availability

Shows how many **read** and **write** execution tickets are still available in the storage engine. Each ticket allows one concurrent operation; when **available** reaches **0**, new operations wait until a ticket is freed.

**Unit:** ticket count (not bytes)

---

### Metrics (same concept, two paths)

**MongoDB 8.x+**  
`serverStatus.queues.execution.read.available`  
`serverStatus.queues.execution.write.available`

**Legacy**  
`serverStatus.wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions.read.available`  
`serverStatus.wiredTiger.concurrentTransactions.write.available`

Both paths queried for compatibility. Usually only one has data per version.

---

### How to read

- Two lines: read and write **available** tickets  
- **stepAfter** reflects discrete ticket changes  
- Typical max ~**128** (dynamic adjustment on 7.0+)

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained **low or zero** → concurrency saturation  
- Correlate with **Current Queue writers / readers** and **Average Operation Latency**

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [Performance tuning — WiredTiger tickets](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/administration/performance-tuning/)

### WiredTiger cache size

**maximum bytes configured** vs **bytes currently in the cache** — WiredTiger internal cache limit and current usage. **Unit:** bytes (per MongoDB docs). Current usage should not exceed the configured maximum.

**Metrics:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.maximum bytes configured` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.bytes currently in the cache`

To change the limit, see `wiredTigerCacheSizeGB` / `storage.wiredTiger.engineConfig.cacheSizeGB` (config in GB; these stats are still bytes).

---

### How to read

- Two lines: configured max and current usage
- WiredTiger often targets ~80% of max under load; sustained saturation → eviction pressure

---

### Troubleshooting

- Usage near max → **Pages Evicted**, **Dirty Cache Bytes**
- Consistently at max → raise `cacheSizeGB` or reduce working set

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

### Pages evicted

Rate of **modified** (dirty) and **unmodified** (clean) cache pages evicted per second. MongoDB docs note unmodified evictions as the main eviction statistic.

**Unit:** pages/s (derivative of cumulative counters)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.modified pages evicted` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.unmodified pages evicted`

---

### How to read

- **Modified pages evicted (dirty)** — evicted after write/reconciliation
- **Unmodified pages evicted (clean)** — discarded without write

---

### Troubleshooting

- Dirty eviction spikes → cache pressure, write latency · **WiredTiger Cache**, **Dirty Cache Bytes**
- Eviction can't keep up → app threads may evict (performance cliff)

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

**tracked dirty bytes in the cache** — modified data in the WiredTiger cache not yet flushed via checkpoint or eviction. Should stay below **bytes currently in the cache**.

- Correlate with **Pages Evicted**, **Checkpoint Write Throughput**

Read/write throughput through WiredTiger's block manager (disk I/O for data files). **Unit:** MB/s (from bytes/s ÷ 1024²) — cumulative byte counters differentiated.

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.block-manager.bytes read` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.block-manager.bytes written`

- **Bytes read** — data read from disk (cache misses)
- **Bytes written** — data written via block manager (eviction, checkpoints)

---

### Troubleshooting

- High reads → cache pressure · **WiredTiger Cache**, **Pages Evicted**
- High writes → checkpoints/eviction · **Checkpoint Write Throughput**, **Disk I/O**

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

Rate of bytes **read into cache** (cold data from disk) and **written from cache** (flush to disk). Overview of WiredTiger cache I/O activity.

**Unit:** B/s (`Bps`) — derivative of cumulative byte counters

**Fields:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.bytes read into cache` · `serverStatus.wiredTiger.cache.bytes written from cache`

---

- **Read into cache** — cache misses / data pulled from disk
- **Written from cache** — dirty data flushed (eviction, checkpoints)

---

### Troubleshooting

- High reads → working set may exceed cache · **WiredTiger Cache**, **Pages Evicted**
- High writes → write load or eviction pressure · **Dirty Cache Bytes**, **WiredTiger Block Manager**

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

### Checkpoint duration

Duration in **milliseconds** of the **most recent** WiredTiger checkpoint. Value updates when a checkpoint completes (~every 60s), then holds until the next.

**Unit:** ms (gauge)

---

**Legacy:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.transaction.transaction checkpoint most recent time (msecs)`  
**MongoDB 8.x+:** `serverStatus.wiredTiger.checkpoint.most recent time (msecs)`

Both queried; usually one path has data per version.

- Single line · rising trend under steady write load → I/O pressure

---

### Troubleshooting

- Increasing duration → I/O saturation · **Checkpoint Write Throughput**, **Disk I/O**, **Average Operation Latency**
- Long checkpoints → possible write stalls

### Docs

- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)
- [WiredTiger storage engine](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/wiredtiger/)

### mongod memory (RSS / virtual)

**mem.resident** (physical RAM) and **mem.virtual** (virtual address space) used by the mongod process.

**Unit:** IEC bytes on chart (auto-scaled GiB/MiB). Source fields are **MiB** in `serverStatus.mem` (`db.serverStatus().mem`); query multiplies by 1024² for display.

**Fields:** `serverStatus.mem.resident` · `serverStatus.mem.virtual`

---

- Two lines: resident vs virtual
- Virtual ≫ resident is normal (mapped files)
- Sudden resident drop → restart · **Server Uptime**
- Tooltip/axis values are auto-scaled; divide by 1024² or compare trends, not raw shell integers

---

### Troubleshooting

- Resident near system RAM → swap risk · **Swap Memory**, **Page Faults**

---

**current**, **active**, and **available** connection counts.

**Unit:** count (gauge)

---

- **Current** — all open connections (incl. idle)
- **Active** — connections running operations
- **Available** — unused connection slots

### Page faults

Rate of `extra_info.page_faults` (cumulative counter since process start). Page faults occur when MongoDB must access data not in physical memory. Per MongoDB docs, limited sporadic faults are normal; sustained high rates often mean the working set exceeds RAM.

**Unit:** page faults/sec (Grafana `ops`)

**Note:** On Windows, hard and soft page faults are both counted; fields in `extra_info` vary by platform.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.extra_info.page_faults`

---

### How to read

- Single line · spikes → memory pressure or cold data access
- Flat near zero → working set mostly in memory

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained high rate → working set > RAM · correlate with **WiredTiger Cache**, **mongod Memory (RSS / Virtual)**, **Swap Memory**
- Spikes during scans/index builds → expected · check query patterns if persistent
- High faults + active swap → add RAM or reduce working set

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — extra_info](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#extra_info)

Rate of **network.numRequests** — distinct client requests received by mongod.

Use with **Network In / Out** to relate request volume to logical byte throughput.

**Unit:** requests/sec (`reqps`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.network.numRequests`

### Average operation latency

Rolling average latency per operation type, derived from cumulative `opLatencies` counters.

**Formula:** `derivative(*.latency) / derivative(*.ops)` → **µs per operation** (same as Δlatency / Δops over each window).

**Unit:** microseconds (`µs`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.opLatencies.reads.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.reads.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.writes.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.writes.ops`
- `serverStatus.opLatencies.commands.latency` · `serverStatus.opLatencies.commands.ops`

---

### How to read

- Three lines: read, write, command average latency
- Spikes → slower operations in that class
- Flat at **0** → no ops in window (idle), not zero latency

---

### Troubleshooting

- Spikes + low **WiredTiger Tickets** → concurrency contention
- Spikes + disk I/O → storage bottleneck · **Page Faults**, **Disk I/O**
- Latency up, ops down → **Operations Latencies Op**, **Operations**
- Commands line often highest → includes admin/aggregate work

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — opLatencies](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.opLatencies)

### Replica members lag

Wall-clock replication lag per member:

**Formula:** `(serverStatus.localTime − members.N.lastAppliedWallTime) / 1000` → **seconds**

Both timestamps are **milliseconds** in FTDC; the query converts the delta to seconds.

**Unit:** seconds (`s`)

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `serverStatus.localTime`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime` … `replSetGetStatus.members.4.lastAppliedWallTime`

Member **N** is the array index in `replSetGetStatus.members` (not necessarily hostname order).

---

### How to read

- One line per member index (0–4)
- **~0** → caught up (primary or healthy secondary)
- Rising trend on a secondary → replication falling behind
- Flat **0** for missing index → no member in that slot

---

### Troubleshooting

- Secondary lag rising → disk I/O, CPU, network on that node · **Opcounters Replica**, **Disk I/O**
- Lag spikes during checkpoints → I/O contention
- Primary throttling → **FlowControl isLagged** · **Replica Members Ping**
- Member down → **Replica Members Health**

---

### Docs

- [replSetGetStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetGetStatus/)
- [serverStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/)

targets.query:

  |> range(start: v.timeRangeStart, stop: v.timeRangeStop)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_measurement"] == "ftdc")

  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["version"] =~ /^${version:regex}$/)
  |> filter(fn: (r) => r["_field"] =~ /replSetGetStatus\.members\.\d+\.lastAppliedWallTime|serverStatus\.localTime/)
  |> drop(columns: ["hostname", "version"])
  |> aggregateWindow(every: v.windowPeriod, fn: last, createEmpty: false)
  |> pivot(rowKey: ["_time"], columnKey: ["_field"], valueColumn: "_value")
  |> map(fn: (r) => ({
      _time: r._time,
      member_0: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.0.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,
      member_1: if exists r["replSetGetStatus.members.1.lastAppliedWallTime"] then (float(v: r["serverStatus.localTime"]) - float(v: r["replSetGetStatus.members.1.lastAppliedWallTime"])) / 1000.0 else 0.0,

### Flow control is lagged

Boolean **`flowControl.isLagged`** — whether flow control is **currently** throttling writes on the **primary**.

**Unit:** 0 = off · 1 = on

**Note:** Primary only; secondaries return placeholders. For **time spent** throttled, see **Flow control lagged time**.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.flowControl.isLagged`

---

### How to read

- **0** → not engaging (even if secondaries lag)
- **1** → primary write rate limited so secondaries can catch up

---

### Troubleshooting

- **1** sustained → **Replica Members Lag**, **Opcounters Replica**, secondary disk/network
- Lag without **1** → lag below `flowControlTargetLagSeconds` threshold

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — flowControl](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.flowControl)

### Replica members ping

**`replSetGetStatus.members.N.pingMs`** — round-trip time in **milliseconds** from **this FTDC host** to each replica set member (repl heartbeat).

**Unit:** milliseconds (`ms`)

**Note:** **N** is the member array index in `replSetGetStatus.members`, not hostname order. Use the **hostname** template variable to pick which mongod’s view of the set you are viewing.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:**

- `replSetGetStatus.members.0.pingMs`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.1.pingMs`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.2.pingMs`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.3.pingMs`
- `replSetGetStatus.members.4.pingMs`

---

### How to read

- One line per member index (**Member 0 ping** … **Member 4 ping**)
- **stepAfter** reflects discrete heartbeat samples
- Low stable values → healthy paths between members
- Spikes → latency or congestion between nodes

---

### Troubleshooting

- Ping rising with **Replica Members Lag** → network may limit replication
- Ping OK but lag high → disk/CPU on secondaries, not network
- Correlate with **TCP** panels (RetransSegs, InSegs/OutSegs) and **Replica Members Health**

---

### Docs

- [replSetGetStatus](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/replSetGetStatus/)

### Flow control lagged time

**Fraction of each window** the primary spent with flow control engaged, from **`flowControl.isLaggedTimeMicros`**.

**Formula:** `derivative(isLaggedTimeMicros, 1s) / 1e6` → 0–100%

**Note:** Primary only. For **on/off now**, see **FlowControl isLagged**.

---

### Metrics

**Fields:** `serverStatus.flowControl.isLaggedTimeMicros`

---

### How to read

- **0%** → no throttling in that window
- **100%** → flow control engaged the entire window
- Spikes → brief throttling bursts

---

### Troubleshooting

- Sustained **>0%** → correlate with **Replica Members Lag**, **FlowControl isLagged**
- High % + rising lag → secondaries cannot keep up · disk/CPU/network

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — flowControl](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.flowControl)

Troubleshooting: sudden drops may indicate blocking -- check 'Current Queue writers / readers' and 'WiredTiger Tickets'. Sudden spikes may cause resource contention. Use alongside 'Average Operation Latency' to distinguish throughput-driven from latency-driven performance issues.

Troubleshooting: high 'returned' with low 'scannedObjects' (from 'Query Executor') indicates efficient queries. High 'returned' with high 'scannedObjects' means poor query targeting. High 'deleted' may indicate TTL index activity or bulk cleanup operations.

Ratio of serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor.scannedObjects to metrics.document.returned, computed as a per-second rate ratio. Per MongoDB docs, scannedObjects is equivalent to totalDocsExamined in explain(); document.returned is the total number of documents returned by queries (serverStatus.metrics.queryExecutor, serverStatus.metrics.document).

How to read: single line showing the scanned-to-returned ratio. A ratio of 1.0 means every scanned document was returned (perfect targeting).

Troubleshooting: ratios significantly above 1.0 indicate queries scanning many documents to return few results -- the classic sign of missing or suboptimal indexes. This is often the number one cause of unnecessary disk I/O and CPU load. Run explain() on slow queries to identify the problem.

Operations **waiting** for the global read or write lock (`globalLock.currentQueue`). Snapshot gauge — not a rate.

**Unit:** count (`short`)

**Note:** On MongoDB 4.2+, these queues are often **0**; use **WiredTiger Tickets** and **Average Operation Latency** for concurrency pressure on modern releases.

---

**Fields:** `serverStatus.globalLock.currentQueue.readers` · `serverStatus.globalLock.currentQueue.writers`

---

### How to read

- Two lines: queued readers vs writers
- Brief spikes can be normal · sustained non-zero → contention

---

### Troubleshooting

- Persistent write queue → **WiredTiger Tickets**, **Average Operation Latency**, **Operations**
- Persistent read queue → long-running reads blocking others
- Always zero but slow DB → focus on tickets/latency, not this panel alone

---

### Docs

- [serverStatus — globalLock](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus/#mongodb-serverstatus-serverstatus.globalLock)

panels.description:
Disk I/O latency per device from systemMetrics.disks.*.read_time_ms and write_time_ms. These counters represent cumulative milliseconds spent on I/O operations (systemMetrics).

How to read: lines showing time spent on reads and writes per device, as a rate (ms of I/O time per second). Values approaching 1000 ms/s indicate the device is saturated.

Troubleshooting: high disk latency directly causes operation latency increases in MongoDB. Correlate with 'Disk Writes and Reads' (IOPS) and 'Disk I/O' (throughput) to understand if latency is from volume or device saturation.
